title_original: Check Point Research Discovers High Risk Vulnerabilities in LiteLLM, One of the Most Widely Used LLM Gateways
description: Check Point Research has discovered two high risk vulnerabilities in LiteLLM, the open source LLM gateway that organizations use to connect their applications to AI providers such as OpenAI, Google and Anthropic. With 97 million downloads per month and over 59,000 GitHub stars, LiteLLM runs inside large enterprises, startups and many of the platforms used to build AI applications. Key Takeaways Check Point Research discovered two high risk vulnerabilities in LiteLLM, tracked as CVE-2026-35029 and CVE-2026-59823. CVE-2026-35029 allowed any user, including those with read only access, to reach administrative functions and take over the gateway. title_original: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host

A flaw in Linux's vhost subsystem lets a local user read and write kernel memory at will and become root across nearly a decade of kernel versions. In one virtualization setup, it lets an untrusted virtual machine write to the host's memory and hijack the program that runs the virtual machine.
